items.stem: How is a WebSocket connection initially established?

options.text: Through an HTTP request that upgrades the connection to the WebSocket protocol
options.rationale: Correct: WebSockets begin with an HTTP upgrade handshake, then switch protocols.

options.text: By opening a raw TCP socket with no HTTP involvement
options.rationale: The standard handshake uses HTTP upgrade, not a bare socket.

options.text: By polling an endpoint every second
options.rationale: Polling is an alternative technique, not how a WebSocket is established.
Email has no role in establishing a WebSocket.

items.explanation: Correct: WebSockets begin with an HTTP upgrade handshake, then switch protocols.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that make a real-time WebSocket application reliable and scalable.

options.text: Reconnect with exponential backoff and resubscribe to prior topics
options.rationale: Correct: backoff reconnection plus resubscription restores state after drops.

options.text: Use a shared backplane so multiple server instances can deliver to all clients
options.rationale: Correct: a backplane lets horizontally scaled servers broadcast consistently.

options.text: Broadcast every message to every connected client
options.rationale: Untargeted broadcasting wastes bandwidth and does not scale.

options.text: Assume one process can hold all connections indefinitely
options.rationale: A single process is a scaling and availability bottleneck.

options.text: Ignore backpressure and buffer without limit
options.rationale: Unbounded buffering under backpressure leads to memory exhaustion.

items.explanation: Correct: backoff reconnection plus resubscription restores state after drops.

items.stem: In a chat application, what is the purpose of the rooms/channels pattern?

options.text: To deliver messages only to clients subscribed to a given room rather than everyone
options.rationale: Correct: rooms scope delivery to interested subscribers.

options.text: To encrypt all messages end to end automatically
options.rationale: Rooms scope delivery; they do not themselves provide encryption.

options.text: To replace the need for a server
options.rationale: Rooms are a server-side delivery concept, not a way to remove the server.

options.text: To guarantee exactly-once delivery with no extra work
options.rationale: Rooms scope recipients but do not by themselves guarantee exactly-once delivery.

items.explanation: Correct: rooms scope delivery to interested subscribers.
